subject: math
title: Multiplication and Division
seo_title: Grade 3 Multiplication and Division Worksheets: Arrays, Equal Groups, Sharing and Grouping (Free, Ontario)
standard_text: Represent multiplication of numbers up to 10 × 10 and division up to 100 ÷ 10, using a variety of tools and drawings, including arrays
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on multiplication and division for the Ontario curriculum: equal groups and arrays, repeated addition, turnaround facts, sharing and grouping, fact families and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for EQAO practice.
key_big: Multiplication counts equal groups. Division splits a total into equal groups.
key_sub: 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. You can multiply in any order: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3. Division undoes multiplication: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 because 3 × 4 = 12.
body_html:
Equal groups and arrays

Multiplication counts equal groups. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4. An array puts the groups in equal rows. Count the rows. Then count one row.

Multiplication is a fast way to do repeated addition. 4 + 4 + 4 is the same as 3 × 4.

Turnaround facts

You can multiply in any order. The answer stays the same. Turn the array a quarter turn: 3 rows of 4 become 4 rows of 3. Both have 12 dots, so 3 × 4 = 4 × 3. If you know one fact, you know two.

Turnaround fact

You know 6 × 9 = 54. What is 9 × 6?

Same numbers, other order. The answer does not change.

Answer: 54

Division: sharing and grouping

Sharing: you know how many groups. Give the items out one at a time. 12 shared on 3 plates is 4 on each plate.

Grouping: you know how many in each group. 12 in groups of 3 makes 4 groups. Both are 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Always start with the total.

Fact families

Division undoes multiplication. 3, 8 and 24 make a fact family of four facts.

Divide with a times fact

What is 42 ÷ 6?

Think: 6 × ☐ = 42. 6 × 7 = 42.

Answer: 7

Use multiplication to check a division. If 56 ÷ 7 = 8, then 7 × 8 must be 56. It is, so the answer is right.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplying (3 × 4 = 7)3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Giving the number of groups, not the total (3 groups of 4 = 3)Count all the items: 3 × 4 = 12
Mixing up groups and items (3 groups of 4 drawn as 4 groups of 3)The first number is the number of groups
Dividing the wrong way (4 ÷ 20 = 5)Start with the total: 20 ÷ 4 = 5
Mixing up sharing and grouping“Among 4” means 4 groups. “Groups of 4” means 4 in each group

faq.q: What multiplication and division do Grade 3 students learn in Ontario?
faq.a: The Ontario math curriculum asks Grade 3 students to show multiplication up to 10 × 10 and division up to 100 ÷ 10 with tools, drawings and arrays. They also learn that division undoes multiplication and that you can multiply in any order.

faq.q: What is the difference between sharing and grouping in division?
faq.a: In sharing you know the number of groups and find how many go in each, like 12 shared on 3 plates. In grouping you know how many go in each group and find the number of groups, like 12 in groups of 3. Both give 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

faq.q: Why do Grade 3 students use arrays for multiplication?
faq.a: An array shows equal rows, so students can see that 3 rows of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Turning the array also shows that 3 × 4 = 4 × 3, and splitting it into rows shows division.

faq.q: Is multiplication and division on the Grade 3 EQAO math test?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, which includes multiplication and division with equal groups and arrays. Mixed word problems like the ones on this page are good practice.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 3, 8 and 24?
items.e: The fact family is 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3. 3 ÷ 24 = 8 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 24, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Which division fact goes with 7 × 8 = 56?
items.e: Division undoes multiplication. 7 groups of 8 make 56, so 56 split into groups of 8 makes 7 groups: 56 ÷ 8 = 7. Start with the biggest number, 56.

items.e: Use multiplication to undo the division: ☐ = 7 × 4 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 9, 10 and 90?
items.e: The fact family is 9 × 10 = 90, 10 × 9 = 90, 90 ÷ 9 = 10 and 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 9 ÷ 90 = 10 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 90, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Which is not in the fact family for 4, 7 and 28?
items.e: The fact family is 4 × 7 = 28, 7 × 4 = 28, 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. 4 ÷ 28 = 7 is wrong: in these facts the biggest number, 28, comes first when you divide.

items.q: Ethan has 45¢ in nickels. A nickel is 5¢. How many nickels does he have?
items.e: How many 5s make 45? 45 ÷ 5. 5 × 9 = 45, so he has 9 nickels.

items.q: Canada geese fly in groups. There are 10 geese in each group. How many geese are in 7 groups?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 10, so multiply: 7 × 10 = 70. Adding 7 + 10 = 17 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Amira has 4 packs of hockey cards. Each pack has 5 cards. She gives 6 cards to her brother. How many cards does she have left?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 5 = 20 cards. Step 2: 20 − 6 = 14 cards left. (3 comes from 4 + 5 − 6.)

items.q: Arjun shares 36 hockey cards equally among 4 friends. How many cards does each friend get?
items.e: Sharing among 4 friends: 36 ÷ 4. 4 × 9 = 36, so each friend gets 9 cards.

items.q: A farm packs 24 small bottles of maple syrup in boxes of 6. How many boxes does it fill?
items.e: Grouping in 6s: 24 ÷ 6. 6 × 4 = 24, so it fills 4 boxes.

items.q: The class sets up chairs in the gym. There are 6 rows. Each row has 8 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: There are 6 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 6 × 8 = 48. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: In gym class, 30 students make teams of 5. How many teams are there?
items.e: Grouping in 5s: 30 ÷ 5. 5 × 6 = 30, so there are 6 teams.

items.q: 32 students go on a field trip. Each parent driver takes 4 students. How many cars are needed?
items.e: Groups of 4: 32 ÷ 4. 4 × 8 = 32, so 8 cars are needed.

items.q: At camp, 7 canoes go out on the lake. Each canoe holds 3 people. How many people can the canoes hold?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 3, so multiply: 7 × 3 = 21. Adding 7 + 3 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Leah has 63 stickers. She puts 9 stickers on each page. How many pages does she fill?
items.e: Groups of 9: 63 ÷ 9. 9 × 7 = 63, so she fills 7 pages.

items.q: At lunch, 8 students sit at each table. There are 9 full tables. How many students are at the tables?
items.e: There are 9 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 9 × 8 = 72. Adding 9 + 8 = 17 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Kai has 3 bags of marbles with 8 marbles in each bag. He shares all the marbles equally among 4 friends. How many marbles does each friend get?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 8 = 24 marbles. Step 2: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, because 4 × 6 = 24. (24 is only step 1.)

items.q: A pack of hockey cards has 8 cards. Owen buys 4 packs. How many cards does he get?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 4 × 8 = 32. Adding 4 + 8 = 12 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Priya reads 10 pages each day. How many days does it take her to read 90 pages?
items.e: How many 10s make 90? 90 ÷ 10 = 9 days. Check: 9 × 10 = 90.

items.q: Each ringette team has 6 players on the ice. 4 teams line up on the ice for a photo. How many players is that?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 6, so multiply: 4 × 6 = 24. Adding 4 + 6 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: There are 56 chairs in the gym. They are in 7 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 56 chairs in 7 equal rows: 56 ÷ 7. 7 × 8 = 56, so each row has 8 chairs.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, the gym teacher puts 40 students into 5 equal lines. Then each line splits into 2 equal teams. How many students are on each team?
items.e: Step 1: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 students in each line. Step 2: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 students on each team. (8 is only step 1. 16 comes from 8 × 2.)

items.q: Noah buys 3 hot chocolates at the rink. Each one costs $2. He pays with a $10 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Step 1: cost: 3 × $2 = $6. Step 2: change: $10 − $6 = $4. ($6 is the cost, not the change.)

items.q: Zoe has 9 toonies. A toonie is worth $2. How much money does she have?
items.e: 9 toonies is 9 groups of $2: 9 × $2 = $18. $11 comes from adding 9 + 2.

items.q: Emma skates 4 laps around the rink each day. How many laps does she skate in 7 days?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 4, so multiply: 7 × 4 = 28. Adding 7 + 4 = 11 only joins the two numbers.
